title: Human-centered AI
summary:
Human-centered AI is the initiative at the intersection of the fields of artificial intelligence and human-computer interaction to develop AI systems in a way that prioritizes human values, needs, and general flourishing. Emphasis is placed on the recognition that artificial intelligence systems are rapidly changing and will continue to influence many aspects of the human experience, in areas ranging from scientific inquiry, governance and policy, labor and the economy, and creative expression. A major stated aim of human-centered AI is to promote the development of AI in ways that augment human capabilities, rather than replacing them.

Organizations and initiatives that take a human-centered approach to AI development focus on frameworks that encourage collaboration between humans and artificial intelligence systems to build towards greater progress, rather than attempting to automate tasks currently handled by humans. Automation and augmentation are not always incompatible; a major aim is towards the automation of rote tasks that would otherwise hinder a human's productivity or creativity, freeing them to direct their energy and intelligence towards higher-level tasks.

Human-centered AI is linked to related endeavors in AI alignment and AI safety, but while these fields primarily focus on mitigating risks posed by unaligned or uncontrollable AI, human-centered AI places significant emphasis on positive augmentation. The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI (HAI) is one prominent group, engaging academics, industry professionals, and policymakers at Stanford University to conduct research and inform policy. Similar groups exist at other universities, including the Chicago Human + AI Lab at the University of Chicago and the Human-Centered AI Lab at the University of Oxford.

Particular attention is paid to mitigating negative effects of AI automation on the livelihoods of the labor force, the use of AI in healthcare fields, and imbuing AI systems with societal values. Applications include data visualization for big data, allowing human engineers to better understand extremely large datasets, and AI-powered sensors to monitor vitals for better responsiveness from healthcare providers.
